papers.title: Less is More: Unbiased Galaxy Clustering from Fewer Merger Trees
papers.authors: Oscar J. Hickman, Sownak Bose, Kai Wang, Carlton M. Baugh, Baojiu Li
papers.abstract: Galaxy clustering could strongly constrain galaxy formation models but is rarely used, because the two-point correlation function (2PCF) requires a complete galaxy catalogue at every point in parameter space. Semi-analytic models (SAMs) process each halo merger tree independently, so running a SAM on $m$ of $k$ disjoint partitions of the trees, each spanning the full box, cuts the cost by $k/m$. Because a halo's galaxies are kept or discarded together, one-halo pairs are diluted less than two-halo pairs, and the naive estimate overstates small-scale clustering by a factor $k/m$. We introduce the Sparse and Unbiased Clustering Estimator (SaUCE), which removes this bias with weights set by $m$ and $k$ alone. It has no free parameters, gives exactly unbiased pair counts, and applies to any catalogue built from a random subset of whole haloes and to any pair-count statistic. Running a SAM on 7 per cent of the P-Millennium merger trees, 68 per cent of random selections recover the full-box $\xi(r)$ at $z=0$ to within 0.05 dex in each bin from 0.03 to $30\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, at a density of $10^{-2}\,h^{3}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$: a fourteen-fold computational saving. The required fraction rises with redshift and as the number density falls, is the same for two model variants, and transfers between boxes through the galaxy and pair counts. The scatter, derived in closed form, is strongly correlated between bins, so a likelihood must use the full covariance. A recipe for choosing the fraction makes the 2PCF affordable for model calibration and simulation-based inference.

The authors introduce the Sparse and Unbiased Clustering Estimator (SaUCE), which derives exact, parameter-free Horvitz-Thompson weights for within-partition and cross-partition pairs to eliminate this clustering bias entirely. Tested on the P-Millennium simulation with the GALFORM SAM, the approach recovers the full-box real- and redshift-space clustering down to small scales using as little as 7% of the merger trees, achieving a more than tenfold computational speedup suitable for MCMC calibration and simulation-based inference.

For a galaxy number density of $\bar{n} = 10^{-2}\,h^3\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$ at $z=0$, processing only 7.3% of the P-Millennium trees recovers the full-box $\xi(r)$ within 0.05 dex across $0.03\text{--}30\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, yielding a 14-fold computational saving.

papers.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
papers.authors: Aliv Sahoo, Fatima Abbasi, Jake McNaughton, Niayesh Afshordi
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

The authors explore whether this horizon-scale physics imprints on cosmic expansion by introducing an extra term $-\Gamma H^2 / \ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ directly into the background Raychaudhuri equation. In the slowly varying logarithm limit, they find closed-form background solutions where the correction acts as dynamical dark energy with a vacuum mode ($w = -1 + 2\sigma/3$) alongside tracking terms sourced by cosmic fluid history. They then evaluate its observational viability using proxy mappings to BBN, CMB, and DESI DR2 data, and investigate field-theoretic completions via the effective field theory of dark energy.

papers.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
papers.authors: POLARBEAR Collaboration : Kam Arnold, Darcy R. Barron, Matthew R. Chu, Nicole Farias, Takuro Fujino, Masaya Hasegawa, Haruaki Hirose, Kailey Hwang, Ethan H. Ish, Jennifer Ito, Brian Keating, Adrian T. Lee, Anto I. Lonappan, Alec Miyashita, Lindsay Ng Lowry, Luke M. Porter, Shahed Shayan Arani, Praween Siritanasak
papers.abstract: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $\Delta \ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2\pi)$ to range from ${\sim}22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to ${\sim}3.5\times10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from ${\sim}2.5$ months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling ${\sim}12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.

Using the Polarbear-2b (PB-2b) receiver of the Simons Array at 90 GHz, the authors employ a novel optical configuration pairing a static ambient quarter-wave plate (QWP) with a continuously rotating cryogenic half-wave plate (HWP) to convert and temporally modulate Stokes $V$ into detector-frame Stokes $U$. They analyze roughly 2.5 months of observations across two low-foreground patches covering $\sim 12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$, tripling the multipole range previously accessed by $V$-mode measurements up to $\ell = 2000$. While the resulting upper bounds remain noise-dominated and several orders of magnitude above standard astrophysical predictions, they demonstrate a practical methodology for targeting circular polarization on ground-based CMB telescopes.
conclusions: Placed 95% confidence upper limits on the CMB circular polarization power spectrum $\ell(\ell+1)C_\ell^{VV}/(2\pi)$ across $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$ (in bins of $\Delta\ell = 100$), ranging from $\sim 22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{CMB}}^2$ at $\ell = 350$ to $\sim 3.5 \times 10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{CMB}}^2$ at $\ell = 1950$.

The measured limits are purely noise-dominated and sit roughly six orders of magnitude above theoretical expectations from Faraday conversion and primordial magnetic fields at 90 GHz.

Demonstrated that combining a static quarter-wave plate with a rotating half-wave plate achieves a net circular polarization conversion efficiency of $\eta_V = 0.528 \pm 0.032$, providing a template for future high-sensitivity instruments.

papers.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
papers.authors: Bayli Hayes, Edgar M. Salazar, Eduardo Rozo, Benedikt Diemer, Calvin Osinga, John Hugon, Vadim Bernshteyn, Ze'ev Vladimir
papers.abstract: In recent work (García et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. Here we introduce the Orbiting-mass ASsIgnment Scheme (OASIS), a fast energy-based algorithm for constructing dynamical halo catalogs. Using single-snapshot information, OASIS achieves $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in orbiting mass estimates relative to the SPARTA particle-tracking algorithm. As an illustration of the applications enabled by OASIS, we use the Quijote and Erebos simulation suites to show that the $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is nearly universal with respect to cosmology, and that it is well described by a modified Press-Schechter form with an effective collapse threshold $\delta_{\rm sc} = 1.54$ at intermediate masses. However, this description fails at high masses.

By exploiting the physical intuition that orbiting particles are virialized and thus possess lower kinetic energy than infalling particles at the same radius, the authors establish a robust, cosmology-dependent energy cut to classify particles. This method provides a computationally efficient alternative to multi-snapshot particle-tracking algorithms like SPARTA, achieving $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in mass estimates. The authors demonstrate that OASIS enables large-scale statistical studies of dynamical halos, revealing that their mass function is nearly universal at $z=0$ but deviates from simple Press-Schechter predictions at high masses.

The kinetic energy cuts are largely universal, showing only a logarithmic dependence on $\Omega_m(z)$ and no significant dependence on halo mass when scaled by $R_{200m}$ and $v_{200m}$.
The $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is approximately universal with respect to cosmology to within $\simeq 5\%$ accuracy.
A modified Press-Schechter model with a collapse threshold $\delta_{sc} = 1.54$ describes the mass function well at intermediate masses but fails at the high-mass end.

papers.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
papers.authors: Jose Agustin Lozano Torres, Axel de la Macorra
papers.abstract: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $\Lambda_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $\Lambda$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $\Lambda_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $\chi^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $\Lambda$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $\Delta\chi^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

papers.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
papers.authors: Peizhi Du, Xiang-Xi Zeng, Jiahang Zhong
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

In this work, the authors derive consistent superhorizon initial conditions for scalar perturbations in general time-dependent backgrounds to avoid non-physical spectral artifacts and construct an explicitly entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model using lattice QCD data. They evaluate SIGW spectra across a broad range of energy scales, including beyond-Standard-Model (BSM) phase transitions, and perform Bayesian parameter inference using the NANOGrav 15-year pulsar timing array dataset.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Neutrinos in NEDE and DRMD Cosmologies: Posteriors, profiles and evidence using CLiENT
papers.authors: Magnus Uggerhøj, Tobias Johannessen, Jeppe Pagaard Thybo, Steen Hannestad, Thomas Tram
papers.abstract:
A large number of extensions of the $\Lambda$CDM model have been proposed as solutions to the Hubble tension, but they are almost always tested separately. Combinations of such models are rarely studied, and one reason is that their parameter spaces are very costly to explore with standard methods. Here we study a combination of two models which have each been proposed as a solution: self-interacting neutrinos (SI$
u$) and the dark radiation matter decoupling (DRMD) of hot new early dark energy. The SI$
u$+DRMD model has twelve cosmological parameters, a bimodal posterior in the neutrino self-interaction and several flat directions in parameter space, and it can only be investigated in detail because we use the likelihood emulator CLiENT. With emulators trained on about $3	imes 10^5$ likelihood evaluations per dataset we obtain posteriors, best fits and profile likelihoods for the model and for the models nested within it, and all quoted $\chi^2$ values are calculated with the true likelihood. We use two data combinations, both with and without the SH0ES calibration: a conservative one consisting of Planck, DESI BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more aggressive one in which the small-scale CMB spectra come from ACT and SPT. With the most aggressive combination, the SI$
u$+DRMD model provides a much better fit than either SI$
u$ or DRMD on its own, and its posterior gives $H_0 = 70.94\pm 0.60$ km/s/Mpc. It lowers the $\chi^2$ of $\Lambda$CDM by 27.6, compared with 9.9 for DRMD and 4.0 for SI$
u$, i.e. by more than the sum of the two ($\Delta$AIC = -15.7 relative to DRMD, in terms of the Akaike information criterion). This shows that combined models can fit the data considerably better than the individual models, and it demonstrates the value of being able to analyse such complex models in detail.

papers.title: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
papers.authors: Hiten, Kanhaiya Lal Pandey, Rajesh Mondal, Subinoy Das, Sharanya Sur
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless $N$-body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare $\Lambda$CDM with four PMF models, $B_0=100$, $130$, $150$, and $170\,\mathrm{pG}$, at $n_B=-2.9$. With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by $\Delta z_{50}\simeq0.50$--$2.14$, with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from $\tau_{\rm e}\simeq0.0547$ for $\Lambda$CDM to $0.0595$--$0.0786$. These simulation-relative offsets span $0.66$--$3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, $\sigma_\tau=0.0073$, and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency $N_{\rm ion}$ is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near $z\sim6$ and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.

Using halo catalogues identified from the simulations, they employ the semi-numerical code ReionYuga to model the spatial distribution of neutral hydrogen, 21-cm brightness temperature fluctuations, and CMB Thomson optical depth $\tau_e$ purely through the structure-formation channel. Their findings highlight how non-linear gravitational collapse converts initial small-scale PMF power into enhanced low-mass halo abundances and earlier reionization, establishing quantitative benchmark signatures for 21-cm experiments like HERA and SKA.
conclusions: PMF-induced power significantly increases early low-mass halo abundances, advancing the reionization midpoint by $\Delta z_{50} \approx 0.50 - 2.14$ relative to $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ for $B_0 = 100 - 170\text{ pG}$ ($n_B = -2.9$).

The integrated Thomson optical depth increases from $\tau_e \approx 0.0547$ in $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ to $0.0595 - 0.0786$ in PMF models, representing simulation-relative shifts of $0.66 - 3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty ($\sigma_\tau = 0.0073$).

Although non-linear gravitational growth attenuates the fractional matter power spectrum contrast between PMF and $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ models over time, the early boost in halo formation preserves strong signatures in 21-cm power spectra and ionization topology.

papers.title: Stable cosmology under flexible covariances: Rescaling and cross-survey correlations in DESI BAO and supernova data
papers.authors: Eleni-Anna Kolonia, Haoye Li, Hanyu Zhang, Niayesh Afshordi
papers.abstract: Combinations of cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and Type Ia supernova (SN) data currently favor evolving dark energy over $\Lambda$CDM at the $\sim 3$--$4\sigma$ level, making it important to test whether this preference could be driven by imperfectly modeled uncertainties. We introduce a phenomenological framework in which the published covariance of each dataset is rescaled by a free parameter and the SN compilations are allowed effective cross-survey correlations. We apply it to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 temperature and polarization data, and a joint likelihood of Pantheon+, Union3, and DES-Dovekie constructed on a common redshift basis. The DESI, Union3, and DES-Dovekie data are consistent with their published covariances, while Pantheon+ shows a mild preference for additional covariance. In all cases the data still allow error bars up to $\sim 1.7$ times larger than published at 95% credibility, yet freeing the rescaling parameters improves the best fit by $\Delta\chi^2 < 1$. Pantheon+ and Union3 exhibit a clear positive effective correlation, $r\simeq 0.4$--$0.5$, plausibly reflecting their shared supernovae; the Pantheon+--DES-Dovekie correlation is weaker and model dependent, and the Union3--DES-Dovekie correlation is consistent with zero. The added covariance freedom broadens the cosmological constraints without shifting them: for the full data combination, the improvement of $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM changes only from $\Delta\chi^2 = 12.8$ to $12.3$ (nominally $3.15\sigma$ to $3.07\sigma$). The preference for evolving dark energy is therefore robust to covariance misestimation of the form considered here.

papers.abstract: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $\mu \propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $\Lambda\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_\delta$ and second-order $b_{\delta^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

papers.title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
papers.authors: Erwin H. Tanin, Sarunas Verner
papers.abstract: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

Cast as model-independent limits on the lifetime of the dark matter particle, the median limit is $\tau > 6.5 \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{s}$. We are also able to detect several expected emission features at high significance, such as atmospheric He I and the 3.3 $\mu$m PAH feature. papers.title: Unidentified Sources in the 4FGL-DR4 Fermi-LAT Catalog as Potential Dark Matter Satellites
papers.authors: Fernando Valenciano, Miguel A. Sánchez-Conde, Jorge Martin Camalich
papers.abstract: The nature of dark matter (DM) remains unknown, standing as one of the most pressing questions in modern physics. We focus on indirect DM detection via gamma-ray emission from annihilating weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). If WIMPs compose DM, annihilation inside these subhalos would generate gamma rays that could be detectable by instruments such as the Fermi-LAT. papers.title: Helicity Decay to Baryons: The Cosmological Evolution of $L_μ-L_τ$ Gauge Fields and Baryogenesis

Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_\chi/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_\chi\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_\chi\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

papers.title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Through Exponential Production Mechanism
papers.authors: Disha Bhatia, Ranjeet Kumar, Rahul Srivastava
papers.abstract: Exponential production of dark matter has been introduced recently as one of the alternatives to the widely studied thermal production of dark matter scenarios. This non-thermal production mechanism leads to the exponential growth in the abundance of the dark matter ($\chi$) through its scatterings with the bath particle ($\xi$), viz. $\chi + \xi \to \chi + \chi$. In our framework, we consider a scalar dark matter $\chi$ charged under $Z_3$ symmetry and bath particle $\xi$ to be standard model singlet and determine the maximum mass of the dark matter using the criteria of perturbativity. We find that dark matter has an upper mass around the ballpark of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV for the cases when the bath particle mass is similar to the dark matter mass. The computations are largely performed with minimal model dependence and will hold in any scenario where the renormalizable couplings driving the exponential growth effectively reduce to $\chi^3\xi$ interactions. Thus, in exponential production of dark matter, we have a possibility of an ultra-heavy dark matter with large couplings, making the scenario phenomenologically interesting. Later, we extend the simplified dark matter model to a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model where the $Z_3$ symmetry is obtained as a residual unbroken subgroup of a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, providing a natural connection with the neutrino sector.

papers.title: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
papers.authors: Ivan Espinoza-Bustamante, Eli S. Rykoff, Eduardo Rozo, Chun-Hao To, Supranta S. Boruah
papers.abstract: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.

papers.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
papers.authors: Sourabh Magare, Anindya, Anupreeta More, Shasvath J. Kapadia
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

papers.title: Conformal Holographic Dark Energy and the Neutrino-Mass Tension
papers.authors: Mario A. Rodríguez-Meza, Jorge L. Cervantes-Cota, Tonatiuh Matos
papers.abstract: Recent DESI results suggest a preference for evolving dark energy (DE) over a cosmological constant, motivating the exploration of alternative models for the background expansion. These data also lead to neutrino-mass constraints close to the lower bounds permitted by oscillation experiments. In this work, we propose and test a conformal holographic dark energy (CHDE) model in which the DE density depends on a power law of the conformal time, characterized by an exponent $n$. The model introduces one additional parameter relative to $\Lambda$CDM and reduces to it in the limit $n=0$. We confront CHDE with BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia datasets, following the combinations used by DESI, and perform parameter inference in both flat and non-flat cosmologies. We find a consistent preference for $n\simeq -0.25$ to $-0.32$, with uncertainties below $\pm 0.1$, and disfavor the $\Lambda$CDM limit at the $4.4$--$4.5\sigma$ level; however, the model-comparison statistics provide no consistent preference for CHDE over $\Lambda$CDM. The resulting neutrino-mass constraints remain compatible with terrestrial limits and yield posterior distributions that peak at positive values, avoiding the negative-mass preference found in $\Lambda$CDM. The CHDE model is therefore consistent with current observational constraints and provides a viable alternative to constant dark energy.

papers.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
papers.authors: S. Ettori (INAF-OAS Bologna)
papers.abstract: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 11 (3) percent (four and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

papers.title: Compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck low-$\ell$ data
papers.authors: Nanoom Lee
papers.abstract: We present a compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data, constructed from the SRoll2 likelihood which provides the tightest constraint on the reionization optical depth $\tau$ to date. The non-Gaussian form of CMB low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods makes them incompatible with Fisher matrix analyses that require an analytic Gaussian $\chi^2$, such as the Fisher-bias formalism and Fisher forecasts. We show that the $\chi^2$ of an offset log-normal likelihood takes a Gaussian form in the log-transformed power spectrum amplitudes, and can therefore serve as a proxy for the true Gaussian likelihood of this variable in Fisher matrix analyses, without any explicit change of variables. Building on this, we compress the SRoll2 likelihood into a small number of piecewise offset log-normal functions and validate it against the full SRoll2 likelihood via MCMC combined with Planck and ACT DR6 data, finding excellent agreement across all $\Lambda$CDM parameters and in extended cosmological models. We further demonstrate that Fisher matrix uncertainty estimates from our compressed likelihood agree well with the full MCMC posteriors. We release our compressed likelihood planck-gaussian-lowl, a lightweight Python package incorporating the compressed low-$\ell$ TT likelihood from previous work, allowing a straightforward incorporation of the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ data into any Gaussian-likelihood-based analysis. The package is publicly available at \href{ this https URL }{ this http URL }.

papers.title: Calibration of CMB Polarisation Using Cross-Experiment Correlations
papers.authors: Claire Rigouzzo, Eugene Lim, Susanna Azzoni, Yiqi Liu
papers.abstract: Parity-violating physics in the Universe can generate correlations between the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) $E$- and $B$-modes, but detecting such signals requires extremely accurate calibration of instruments. We describe a data-driven method to calibrate the relative polarisation angle between CMB experiments using cross-correlations of observations over a common sky region. Unlike standard self-calibration approaches, this method does not assume vanishing isotropic cosmic birefringence or primordial $EB$ correlations when estimating the relative misalignment angle, and therefore preserves sensitivity to parity-violating physics. As a proof of concept, we forecast the performance of this method using the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) as a calibrated reference. If they can be calibrated to an uncertainty of $0.08^\circ$, as anticipated from the SO wire grid calibration system, we show that the SO Large Aperture Telescope and Planck could be calibrated to uncertainties of $0.10^\circ$ and $0.17^\circ$, respectively, at $\sim 145$ GHz. This approach relies on the availability of at least one well-calibrated instrument, and provides a complementary path to improving polarisation calibration across experiments, enabling more robust searches for parity-violating physics in the CMB, such as cosmic birefringence.

papers.title: Impact of lensing magnification on the power spectrum turnover
papers.authors: Yolanda Dube, Roy Maartens, Bikash R. Dinda, Sêcloka L. Guedezounme, Sheean Jolicoeur
papers.abstract: The turnover scale $k_0$ of the matter power spectrum -- and consequently of the standard galaxy power spectrum monopole -- encodes a fundamental signature of matter-radiation equality and constitutes an important standard ruler independent of baryon acoustic oscillations. In principle, we can detect the turnover at multiple redshifts and amplify the signal by stacking redshift bins. However, in spectroscopic surveys reaching high redshifts, such as the Euclid H$\alpha$ survey and the proposed MegaMapper Lyman-break galaxy survey, the monopole of the observed galaxy power spectrum receives a scale-dependent correction from lensing magnification. This can modify the signal shape and shift the turnover scale, undermining its use as a standard ruler. Using mock surveys similar to Euclid and MegaMapper, we forecast this shift and the consequent bias in the turnover scale that is recovered from the mock data. The shift in the turnover scale grows with redshift, leading to a maximum bias of $\sim 0.4\sigma$ (Euclid-like) and $\sim 3.6\sigma$ (MegaMapper-like). To avoid a bias $>1\sigma$, the maximum redshift for a MegaMapper-like survey is $z\approx 2.9$. Data in the remaining range $2.9\lesssim z\le 5$ does not directly provide a reliable recovery of the intrinsic turnover. In fact, we find that the turnover vanishes in a MegaMapper-like survey for $z\gtrsim 3.7$. Our results show that the lensing correction to the monopole should be included and carefully modelled when surveys are used to measure the cosmological turnover at high redshifts.

papers.title: Cosmological evolution with decaying dark matter: an integral-equation approach
papers.authors: Nanoom Lee, Anna Bencke, Marc Kamionkowski, José Luis Bernal
papers.abstract: We present CLASSIER-DDM, an extension of the Boltzmann solver CLASSIER that implements the decaying dark matter (DDM) model via its integral-equation approach. The code handles generic two-body decays of a dark matter particle into two lighter decay products with arbitrary masses, naturally encompassing both massless (dark radiation) and massive (warm) decay products, with their perturbations evaluated via integral equations solved iteratively. We describe the numerical implementation in detail, including the background evolution, the iterative perturbation evolution, and a small-scale analytic approximation. A modest number of iterations is sufficient to achieve sub-$0.1\%$ convergence in the matter power spectrum and the CMB lensing power spectrum across the observationally relevant parameter space. We find that a hundred momentum bins for the decay product perturbations are sufficient to achieve $\mathcal{O}(0.1\%)$ accuracy in the matter power spectrum today up to $k \sim 3\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. The code achieves $\mathcal{O}(1\,{\rm min})$ runtimes per evaluation, requiring neither a Boltzmann hierarchy nor any fluid approximation, making parameter estimation with the DDM model numerically tractable. We also discuss the impact of DDM on cosmological observables, focusing on the case of two massive decay products. This work further establishes the integral-equation approach as a versatile and efficient framework for modeling non-cold relics in cosmological perturbation theory.

papers.title: Cosmological constraints on single-field inflation models from ACT/SPT data and observations at sub-Mpc scales
papers.authors: Qing-Yang Wang, Jing-Zhi Zhou, Fei-Yu Chen, Zhi-Chao Li
papers.abstract: We investigate single-field inflation models that can produce large curvature perturbations at sub-Mpc scales while remaining consistent with cosmological observations across multiple regimes. We highlight the tension between generating enhanced small-scale perturbations and maintaining agreement with the scalar spectral index $n_s$ measured by ACT and SPT, which disfavors several conventional single-field inflation models. To address this issue, we propose three viable classes of inflationary potentials: bump/dip-modified, step-like, and double-inflection-point. Each can sufficiently amplify primordial perturbations while predicting $n_s$ that lie within the $2\sigma$ range of current observational bounds. In addition, we examine the primordial power spectra predicted by these models and constrain their parameter spaces using cosmological observations at different scales, including CMB, BAO, PBH, PTA, and CMB-distortion. Our results show that some of the models considered can simultaneously satisfy the ACT/SPT constraints and account for the current PTA observations, although doing so while respecting the constraints on the PBH abundance remains challenging.

papers.title: A self-supervised machine learning approach to identify instrumental systematics in 21cm Cosmology
papers.authors: Ajith Sampath
papers.abstract: The primordial sound waves in the baryon-photon plasma are imprinted on the large-scale galaxy distribution as Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), serving as a cosmological standard ruler to constrain dark energy and the Hubble parameter. The upcoming 21cm intensity-mapping arrays are designed to map the 21cm emission across large volumes and measure the BAO scale. However, radio interferometers suffer from instrumental systematics that can hinder detection of the cosmological 21cm signal by leaking bright foregrounds into the signal-dominated modes. This work aims to demonstrate that a self-supervised model can predict the instrument systematic state (here, the amplitude of a spectral ripple in the beam width) in interferometric visibilities and potentially disentangle the instrument from the sky without a forward model. Based on the fact that an instrument stays the same as the sky rotates in a drift-scan observation, and that the same sky is observed under different instrument states, we train a convolutional autoencoder to compress the information in the simulated visibilities and separate this information into instrument-only and sky-only latent vectors. The result shows excellent prediction of the unknown instrument systematic for 15 held-out instrument states with $R^2 = 0.9975$ with a linear probe, against $R^2 = -3.55$ for a random-encoder baseline. The instrument-latent carries no detectable sky signal, as measured with a total-power sky proxy, for any held-out test data. The sky-latent vector and instrument-latent vector show partial separation but not complete disentanglement, identifying sky-latent purity as the primary open problem. The results show the ability of the model to recognize the systematic and show a promising path towards an ML-based foreground cleaning pipeline. Full instrument-sky disentanglement constitutes the natural next step.

papers.title: Short-term optical monitoring of quadruply imaged quasars
papers.authors: L. J. Goicoechea, V. N. Shalyapin, A. Esteban-Gutiérrez, R. Gil-Merino, M. Serra-Ricart
papers.abstract: We present two case studies to demonstrate that short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quadruply imaged quasars (quads) reveal their astrophysical potential. Using the Liverpool Telescope and the third facility of the Two-meter Twin Telescope (TTT3), we monitored the quads QSO 2237+0305 and PS J0147+4630 in the gr bands between July 2025 and January 2026. For QSO 2237+0305, the resulting light curves revealed microlensing variability over a timescale of ~150 days. The g-band difference light curve between images A and B was then used to reliably constrain the half-light radius of the g-band source within the 3.5-16 lt-day range (1{\sigma} confidence level). For PS J0147+4630, we derived new constraints on the AB and AC time delays from the r-band light curves of the ABC images in an arc-like configuration, obtaining 2{\sigma} uncertainties of ~2 days. These constraints were used to shed light on the lensing mass distribution. Overall, our results validate the design of short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quads as valuable astrophysical tools in the era of large-scale surveys. The proof of concept relies on observations with ground-based 2mclass telescopes that lack sophisticated systems to correct for optical distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence, and we indicate the astro-photometric properties of the targets and the monitoring strategies needed to achieve success with these telescopes. Additionally, this work represents the first validation of the TTT3 facility for precision photometric monitoring of gravitationally lensed quasars.

To ensure a robust validation of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) analysis using Ly$\alpha$ forests, we have made significant updates compared to DR1 to both the mocks and the analysis framework used in the validation. In particular, we present CoLoRe-QL, a new set of Ly$\alpha$ mocks that use a quasi-linear input power spectrum to incorporate the non-linear broadening of the BAO peak. We have also increased the number of realisations used in the validation to 400, compared to the 150 realisations used in DR1. Finally, we present a detailed study of the impact of quasar redshift errors on the BAO measurement, and we compare different strategies to mask Damped Lyman-$\alpha$ Absorbers (DLAs) in our spectra. The BAO measurement from the Ly$\alpha$ dataset of DESI DR2 is presented in a companion publication.

papers.title: Measuring the Evolution of Bulge, Disk and Colour Gradients in HST Observations of Galaxies with 3D Modelling
papers.authors: N. Welikala, L. Miller, A. N. Taylor, G. Congedo
papers.abstract: We measure galaxy structural properties and colour gradients using HST images to trace the evolution of galaxy components. We develop and apply a physically motivated 3D bulge+disk modelling framework, jointly fitting the components in 2505 galaxies in GOODS-South across seven bands (bvizYJH) to $I_{\rm AB}=25.5$, accounting for different component ellipticities and inclination-dependent dust extinction. Extinction strongly affects structural parameters and colour gradients in $\sim$26% of the sample - primarily edge-on galaxies with central obscuration (B-band face-on optical depth $\tau \simeq 4$) that reveal clear bulge components in the near-infrared. Despite irregular morphologies, the model captures observed colour gradients well. Bulges at $z \sim 1$ differ markedly from $z \sim 0$, with typical Sérsic index $n \sim 1.0$ and bulge-to-disc size ratio $R_{\rm e}/h_{\rm d} \sim 0.15$, suggesting most galaxies host pseudo-bulges formed via secular evolution. Galaxy ellipticity correlates strongly with disk scale-length. We trace bulge and disk evolution from $z \sim 0$ to $z \sim 2.5$: bulges are redder than disks (observed-frame) at $z < 1.4$, but colours converge at higher redshifts and fainter magnitudes. Redder galaxies show redder cores relative to their outskirts, and brighter galaxies have redder cores. These results provide new measurements of bulge and disk structural properties at $z \sim 1$ and observational constraints on their evolution, while also providing empirically motivated input distributions for assessing colour gradient systematics in weak lensing surveys.

papers.title: Gravitational open effective field theory of inflation
papers.authors: Perseas Christodoulidis, Jinn-Ouk Gong
papers.abstract: We construct a gravitational open extension of the effective field theory of inflation in the Schwinger-Keldysh framework. While physical symmetries allow many open operators in the Schwinger-Keldysh action, most of them overconstrain the equations of motion, yielding inconsistent dynamics. We identify a minimal open operator compatible with propagating scalar and tensor modes and build a local gravitational action, recovering known dissipative models of inflation.

papers.title: Weinberg Angle, Neutron Abundance in BBN, and Lifetime
papers.authors: Cheng Tao Yang, Johann Rafelski
papers.abstract: We present state of the art kinetic theory determination of the neutron abundance available for the Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). Our work is motivated by the study of the neutron lifespan measured in the laboratory and the unknown strength of weak interactions coupling constant $G_\mathrm{F}$ at finite temperature in the primordial Universe. We draw attention to the relevant dependence of $G_\mathrm{F}$ on the symmetry breaking Weinberg angle $s^2_\mathrm{W}$, a free parameter in the standard model of particle physics. We establish how the value of $s^2_\mathrm{W}$ by way of $G_\mathrm{F}$ modification influences neutron abundance available for BBN and neutron lifetime.

papers.title: Multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves from PBH-assisted leptogenesis
papers.authors: Debasish Borah, Nayan Das
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of probing non-thermal leptogenesis with multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves (GW) by considering heavy right-handed neutrino (RHN) produced from primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation to be responsible for generating the required lepton asymmetry. The decay of RHN also produces a GW spectrum due to graviton bremsstrahlung with the corresponding amplitude being enhanced for heavier RHN. The presence of an ultra-light PBH dominated epoch not only ensures sufficient production of RHNs, but also keeps the leptogenesis scenario free from strong washout problem of thermal leptogenesis at very high scale. In addition, the PBH dominated epoch also helps in generating a gravitational bremsstrahlung spectrum distinct from the stochastic GW background from the thermal bath. Finally, PBH evaporation also brings two separate sources of GW via density perturbation and graviton emission via Hawking evaporation. For the most optimistic scenario with very high scale seesaw consistent with neutrino mass and leptogenesis, this leads to a multi-peaked GW spectrum with peak frequencies lying in the MHz-EHz range.

papers.title: Long-term 3+1 simulations of primordial black hole formation during radiation domination
papers.authors: Zhuan Ning, Rong-Gen Cai, Shao-Jiang Wang, Chul-Moon Yoo
papers.abstract: We develop an efficient three-dimensional numerical-relativity framework for primordial black-hole (PBH) formation from superhorizon curvature perturbations in a radiation-dominated Universe. We implement flux-conservative relativistic hydrodynamics in the adaptive-mesh-refinement code GRChombo and introduce a cosmologically scaled Gamma-driver that allows the cosmic-time step to grow in proportion to the scale factor. For a representative long-term simulation, the scaled driver preserves the apparent-horizon mass evolution and constraint behavior while reducing the number of coarse-level advances by a factor of approximately $94$ relative to the standard driver. We also construct a conformal-time version of the moving-puncture gauge as a consistency check. Applying the framework to a spherical Gaussian curvature profile, we find a collapse threshold $\mu_c \simeq 0.7958$ and approximate critical mass scaling, consistent with previous spherically symmetric results. We further fit the late-time PBH mass growth to the Zel'dovich--Novikov accretion law, demonstrating that the code can follow both near-critical collapse and long-term post-formation evolution in three dimensions. The framework provides a foundation for future studies of PBH formation beyond spherical symmetry.

papers.title: Cosmological Constrained Axion-Portal Inelastic Dark Matter for the LZ Event
papers.authors: Haipeng An, Fei Gao, Jia Liu, Minghao Liu, Changlong Xu
papers.abstract: The recent high-recoil candidate event reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates dark-matter scenarios with nonstandard kinematics and momentum-dependent interactions. We study a two-state inelastic dark-matter model in which $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$ couple off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons and photons. Unlike treatments that assume only one dark-matter state is present today, we track the cosmological evolution of both states. The excited state $\chi_2$ is sufficiently long-lived to survive to the present, with its relic fraction determined by the dark-sector conversion process $\chi_2\chi_2\leftrightarrow\chi_1\chi_1$. We find that this fraction depends strongly on the Lorentz structure of the DM--ALP interaction. Scalar transition couplings lead to nonperturbative conversion rates with a pronounced resonant structure, yielding a final excited-state fraction that varies nonmonotonically with the mediator mass, from $f_2\sim10^{-4}$ to approximately $1/2$ over the parameter range studied. The relative importance of endothermic and exothermic scattering is therefore parameter dependent. By contrast, pseudoscalar transition couplings preserve $f_2\simeq1/2$, yielding recoil spectra dominated by exothermic $\chi_2 N\to\chi_1 N$ down-scattering for the benchmarks considered. Benchmark spectra in all four scenarios can peak near the observed recoil energy of $250\,\mathrm{keV}$. Our results demonstrate that the dominant direction of inelastic scattering in direct detection can be dynamically selected by the early-Universe evolution of the dark sector. With additional data, annual modulation measurements could distinguish these scenarios. We further show that the ALP portal can be directly probed at colliders.

papers.title: Breaking the AGB Color Degeneracy with Variability and H$_2$O: A Consistent Picture of AGB Chemistry, Dust, and the J-Region Across Environments
papers.authors: Caroline D. Huang, Massimo Marengo, Antonio Capodagli, Adam G. Riess, Louise Breuval, Stefano Casertano, Patricia A. Whitelock, Gagandeep S. Anand, Randall K. Smith, Wenlong Yuan
papers.abstract: Resolved asymptotic giant branch (AGB) populations present many observational puzzles. We consider three often treated separately: photometric C/O classification boundaries must be redrawn empirically in new environments; hydrostatic model grids are too blue in bands sampling H2O absorption; and J-region (JAGB) luminosities can differ between fields of a single galaxy. Pulsation connects them into a coherent picture. Using SPHEREx spectroscopy of AGB stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) with JWST/NIRCam photometry and HST time-series of the SN Ia host M101, placed on a common scale by synthetic photometry, we investigate how AGB variability, surface chemistry, and circumstellar dust depend on environment. We develop an F182M index sensitive to 1.9$\mu$m H2O absorption that chemically classifies variable AGB stars and reveals oxygen-rich (O-rich) stars degenerate with carbon-rich (C-rich) stars in broadband colors. Because these features arise in extended atmospheric layers, hydrostatic grids struggle to reproduce them. Pulsation and circumstellar dust are asymmetrically linked: nearly all stars with substantial infrared excess are variable, while many variables show little dust. This supports mass loss initiated by pulsation and enhanced by dust formation. Variable O-rich AGB stars in M101 are up to ~0.7 mag redder than their LMC counterparts in dust-sensitive colors, consistent with more efficient silicate-dust production at higher metallicity, while C-rich populations depend less on environment. Color windows that select C-rich stars cleanly in the LMC are therefore 33-68% O-rich in the metal-rich M101. This challenges the J-region's universality as a standard candle while evading standard self-consistency checks. We recommend combining variability, or the infrared excess that implies it, with photometry of molecular features to improve AGB classification at 0.75-5.0$\mu$m.

papers.title: Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
papers.authors: Juan P. Luengas, Maxim Pospelov, Harikrishnan Ramani
papers.abstract: One of the most convincing realizations of particle dark matter is provided by models based on electroweak multiplets. The lightest neutral state of such a multiplet can be a stable Majorana fermion or a real scalar, and its phenomenology is governed by two parameters: the dark matter mass and the mass splitting $\{m_\chi,\delta\}$. The sub-MeV range for $\delta$ is particularly important as it allows for a large inelastic scattering cross section. In this paper, we analyze solar capture, energy loss, and annihilation of scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplet dark matter, generalizing earlier results for the Higgsino to other representations. We find that, while the case of a doublet is somewhat special, higher representations behave in a self-similar way. For the higher multiplets, IceCube results constrain the splitting to $\delta \gtrsim 350$ keV for all dark matter masses up to $100$ TeV. Assuming thermal freeze-out and a Standard Halo Model velocity distribution, this rules out most models of electroweak dark matter as a possible origin of the single high-recoil event reported by the LZ collaboration. We also show that a high-velocity tail in the dark matter distribution, such as that induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud, raises the splitting preferred by the LZ event above the solar bounds for many of the multiplets.
